purpose: Research frameworks for challenging GCI recommendations. Principles are paraphrased summaries of each person's widely documented public doctrine, not quotations and not trading instructions. No investor in this library endorses any GCI recommendation.
rules: Weight evidence by distinct lens, never by fame or by how many famous names share a view.
Disagreement between schools is surfaced, not averaged away; the Judgment Reviewer must answer every CHALLENGE.
Doctrines that depend on leverage, derivatives, activism, concentration or private markets are STUDY_ONLY for actions under the current policy.
Past results of these investors are not evidence that GCI will achieve similar results.

schools.value: Buy below conservatively estimated worth; demand a margin of safety.
schools.quality_growth: Own excellent businesses for a long time; avoid overpaying.
schools.index: Own the market cheaply and broadly; minimise costs and behaviour errors.
schools.contrarian: Buy when others are most pessimistic; sell into euphoria.
schools.macro: Position for economic cycles, liquidity, rates and currencies.
schools.quant: Act only on statistically validated, tested patterns; systematic execution.
schools.risk_management: Survive first: position limits, drawdown control, capital preservation.

investors.name: Warren Buffett

principles.text: Estimate intrinsic value and buy with a margin of safety.
Stay within your circle of competence; understand what you own.
Time and patience compound; avoid unnecessary activity.
For most non-professional investors, a low-cost index fund is a sensible choice.

investors.caution: Berkshire's results rely on scale, insurance float and private deals that a $40 account cannot replicate.

investors.name: Charlie Munger

principles.text: Invert: list how this could fail, then avoid those paths.
Use a latticework of mental models; avoid obvious stupidity rather than seeking brilliance.
Know the edge of your competence.

investors.caution: Late-career Munger favoured extreme concentration; that part is STUDY_ONLY here.

investors.name: Benjamin Graham

principles.text: Mr. Market offers prices; you need not accept them. Do not let price moves dictate your judgment.
Margin of safety is the central concept of investment.
The defensive investor should diversify and keep a balance between stocks and high-grade bonds.

investors.caution: Classic net-net bargains are rare in large modern markets.

investors.name: Peter Lynch

principles.text: Be able to explain what you own and why in plain words.
Earnings growth drives long-run returns; do not overpay for it.

investors.caution: Stock-picking research cost is prohibitive at $40.

investors.name: John Bogle

principles.text: Costs compound against you; minimise fees.
Own the whole market; diversify across thousands of securities.
Stay the course; avoid trading on emotion.

sources: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing (2007)
investors.caution: Index investing accepts full market drawdowns.

investors.name: Philip Fisher

principles.text: Assess management and business quality deeply before buying.
Hold outstanding businesses for many years.

investors.caution: Scuttlebutt research is labour-intensive; not economic for small positions.

investors.name: Howard Marks

principles.text: Know where we stand in the cycle; risk is highest when it feels lowest.
Second-level thinking: what is priced in, and what does the consensus miss?
Defensive investing: avoiding losers matters more than finding winners.

investors.caution: Distressed-credit strategies themselves are STUDY_ONLY here.

investors.name: Seth Klarman

principles.text: Focus on downside first; demand a margin of safety.
Holding cash is acceptable when bargains are absent.

investors.caution: Baupost's opportunity set includes private and illiquid assets.

investors.name: Li Lu

principles.text: Do deep fundamental research and hold a few high-conviction businesses for a long time.
Long horizons let business value, not sentiment, determine outcomes.

sources: Civilization, Modernization, Value Investing and China (2020)
investors.caution: Concentration is a policy exception at GCI's current size and research budget.

investors.name: Mohnish Pabrai

principles.text: Seek asymmetric bets: heads I win, tails I don't lose much.
Clone sound ideas from proven investors rather than inventing new ones.
Few bets, big bets, infrequent bets.

investors.caution: Cloning requires verifying the original thesis, not copying positions blindly.

investors.name: Rakesh Jhunjhunwala

principles.text: Long-term conviction in a growing economy's equity market.
Respect market cycles; volatility is the price of long-run growth.

investors.caution: Also traded actively with leverage at times; that part is STUDY_ONLY. Direct Indian equities need account eligibility checks.

investors.name: Radhakishan Damani

principles.text: Business economics and cost discipline drive long-run value.
Patient capital allocation over decades.

sources: Secondary profiles (he gives few public statements)
investors.caution: Doctrine is inferred from his record more than from his own statements; weight it lightly.

investors.name: Walter Schloss

principles.text: Buy asset-backed cheap stocks, keep it simple, and diversify widely.
Avoid debt and avoid stories you cannot verify.

sources: Factors Needed to Make Money in the Stock Market (Schloss, 1994)

investors.name: Sir John Templeton

principles.text: Search globally; buy at the point of maximum pessimism.
Diversify across countries; no market is always the best.

investors.caution: Buying into extreme pessimism needs a long horizon and nerve.

investors.name: Anthony Bolton

principles.text: Contrarian stock selection backed by company research.
Valuation discipline; know why something is cheap.

investors.caution: His later China fund had difficult results; contrarian calls can be early or wrong.

investors.name: Terry Smith

principles.text: Buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing.
Minimise trading and costs.

investors.caution: Quality stocks can be expensive; 'don't overpay' is the hard part.

investors.name: Francisco García Paramés

principles.text: Independent judgment; long holding periods.
Go where value is, regardless of country.

investors.caution: Value tilts can underperform for many years.

investors.name: Akira Mori

principles.text: Patient ownership and stewardship of long-lived real assets.

investors.caution: A real-estate operator, not a public-markets investor; use only as a stewardship lens.

investors.name: Jim Simons

principles.text: Trade only on patterns that survive rigorous statistical testing.
Systematic execution; models over gut feel.

sources: The Man Who Solved the Market (Zuckerman, 2019)
investors.caution: Medallion's methods are proprietary. The transferable lesson is the testing discipline, not any strategy.

investors.name: Ray Dalio

principles.text: Diversify across uncorrelated return streams, not just across securities.
Understand the economic machine: credit, liquidity and debt cycles.
Stress-test beliefs; seek out people who disagree.

investors.caution: Risk-parity implementations use leverage; that part is STUDY_ONLY.

investors.name: George Soros

principles.text: Reflexivity: prices shape fundamentals as well as reflect them.
Know what would prove you wrong, and act quickly when it happens.

investors.caution: Large leveraged macro bets are prohibited by policy.

investors.name: Stanley Druckenmiller

principles.text: Liquidity and central-bank policy drive markets.
Size up only when the opportunity is asymmetric; protect capital otherwise.

investors.caution: His concentration and leverage are STUDY_ONLY.

investors.name: David Tepper

principles.text: Distressed assets can offer outsized reward for risk when fear peaks.

sources: Public interviews and financial press profiles
investors.caution: Distressed-credit investing needs specialised access and analysis.

investors.name: Ken Griffin

principles.text: Institutional risk systems and portfolio discipline across strategies.

investors.caution: Multi-strategy platforms run on scale and leverage.

investors.name: Cliff Asness

principles.text: Value and momentum premia appear across markets and asset classes; diversify across factors.
Momentum: trends tend to persist in the short-to-medium term.

sources: Value and Momentum Everywhere (Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen, Journal of Finance, 2013)
investors.caution: Factor premia can disappear for a decade.

investors.name: Israel Englander

principles.text: Strict risk budgets; independent strategies cut quickly at drawdown limits.

investors.caution: GCI's own analogue is the research-budget and drawdown controls.

investors.name: Paul Tudor Jones

principles.text: Capital preservation first; play great defence.
Respect trends; be careful buying below the 200-day moving average.

investors.caution: Short-term trading itself is not GCI policy.

investors.name: Michael Steinhardt

principles.text: Variant perception: hold a well-founded view that differs from consensus.

investors.caution: A variant view needs evidence, not just disagreement.

principles.text: Disciplined position sizing; decide where you are wrong before entering.

investors.name: Louis Bacon

principles.text: Geopolitical awareness and downside protection in global macro.

investors.caution: Few primary statements; weight lightly.

principles.text: Computational, quantitative research; act on measurable edges.
Data science and statistical modelling; the scientific method applied to markets.
Hard risk limits and performance accountability.
Rates and currency analysis with capital protection.
Concentrated research into businesses with durable shareholder economics.

investors.name: Bill Ackman

principles.text: High-conviction fundamental positions, sometimes with activism.

sources: Pershing Square annual reports and investor presentations
investors.caution: Concentrated positions have produced both large gains and large losses.

investors.name: Masayoshi Son

principles.text: Long-horizon technology bets carry venture-scale risk; concentration and leverage magnify losses as well as gains.

sources: SoftBank Group annual reports and earnings presentations
investors.caution: Included mainly for concentration-risk lessons.

principles.text: Broad global diversification at low cost, governed by clear rules.
Multi-decade horizon and stewardship.

investors.name: Edward O. Thorp

principles.text: Bet only with a measurable edge.
Size positions by the Kelly criterion, or a fraction of it; with no edge, the optimal bet is zero.
Most investors are better served by index funds.

sources: Beat the Market, with Sheen Kassouf (1967)
